commenti.body: The end is punctuated by Dr. Strangelove standing up, and a montage of nukes: The Nazis and nuclear holocaust. The past and future threats coming together. I think it’s a way of showing the cyclical nature of the world conflict and is the film’s commentary on the Cold War. The Soviet and US will keep doing this until the end of the world. And it’s silly, horrifying, but somehow beautiful.

It's to show that nothing changes. The people who caused Armageddon will not learn and will keep making the same mistakes. 

And maybe generals and leaders should be given ED pills so they have fewer insecurities
Agreed. “I can *walk!*” is one of my favorite endings to any movie. Sellers’ performance(s) is incredible and it’s just such a perfect moment of absurdity to end the film on.

To me it it highlighted the sometimes very real assumptions we have about people in leadership positions; that they're self-obsessed, off-based, and motivated by their own self-interests rather than the greater good. Or that the sometimes needless competitiveness between countries distracts us from what's really important: avoiding all out nuclear war for instance.

Everyone in the war room acts with such little urgency that it's sometimes maddening to watch. Coupled with how they spend their final moments theorizing how to survive and even getting horny over the idea of repopulating the world, the ending is like an dramatic underline to its central satirical message.
Yes but what really got me was when General Turgidson yells “WE CANT HAVE A MINESHAFT GAP” it really nailed down the absurdity of the whole situation for me and I burst out laughing.
